prompt: A Ferris wheel seat follows $h = 18\sin(x) + 22$ metres. What is the HIGHEST height the seat reaches, in metres?
hint: Sine can never be bigger than $1$, so the biggest $18\sin(x)$ can be is $18$.

hints.text: Sine can never be bigger than $1$, so the biggest $18\sin(x)$ can be is $18$.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try $h = 2\sin(x) + 5$. The biggest sine is $1$, so the top is $2 \times 1 + 5 = 7$. Same two steps work for $18$ and $22$.

explanation: The wave climbs highest when $\sin(x) = 1$, which happens at $x = 90^\circ$.
$h = 40$ metres. That is the midline $22$ plus the amplitude $18$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Picture the wheel
steps: The centre of the wheel is 22 m above the ground and the radius is 18 m.
The very top of a wheel is one radius above its centre: 22 + 18 = 40 m.

alternativeExplanations.title: Make a small table
steps: x = 135°: back down to about 34.7. The peak is at 90°, giving 40 m.
